title: Stream handoff recovery and partial-output conciliation for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent truncation of SSE streaming responses from the Hosted API with no clear resume path. In several cases clients received partial JSON or text fragments and were unable to resume to receive the rest of the generation. Incidents spanned Hosted, and surfaced similar symptoms for Dedicated customers using the hosted control-plane for routing. This ticket scopes investigation, temporary mitigations, and a permanent fix that ensures resumability and safe stitching of partial outputs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open an SSE stream against v1/generate with a long generated output (>> 2k tokens). 2) Apply an idle TCP timeout at an intermediate proxy between client and our frontend (simulate 60s idle close). 3) Observe connection closed mid-chunk and client receives truncated final data frame. 4) Attempt client-side resume using previously observed stream-id/token; existing server path rejects with resume_token_mismatch or returns duplicate tokens causing inconsistent dedup behavior.
investigation_notes:
- Initial logs showed 503/502 traces correlating with CloudLB idle timeouts (default 75s) when clients paused reading (slow consumers).
- Frontend kept ephemeral stream state but relied on an in-memory resume token that changed when a reconnect race occurred.
- Partial-fragment writes were not assigned stable chunk IDs, so stitcher could not reconcile whether a resumed stream should request missing sequences.
- Some Dedicated customers using private routing saw same problem due to their proxies closing connections and not forwarding last-ACK semantics.
- Reproducer harness created in staging with tcpkill/iptables to simulate abrupt mid-chunk drops.
root_cause: Two primary failures combined: (1) an unstable resume token algorithm that encoded volatile runtime pointers (heap address + ephemeral sequence) causing token mismatch on reconnect; (2) lack of durable, per-stream chunk sequence IDs persisted long enough for short resume windows. When LB/proxy closed idle connections mid-chunk, clients could reconnect but server rejected resumes because token didn't match the updated ephemeral state. Stitching logic was optimistic and expected idempotent replays, which failed without stable chunk identifiers.
fix:
1) Replace resume token with a stable HMAC over (stream_id, persistent_sequence_base, model_version) and a short TTL. This avoids volatile pointer encoding.
2) Emit monotonic chunk IDs (stream_id + sequence_number) for every flush boundary and persist last-committed sequence in a small, highly available store (in-memory with replication and tombstones) for 2 minutes to support short resumes.
3) Update stitcher to be tolerant: accept overlapping sequences and dedupe on chunk IDs. Add a backfill endpoint (/v1/streams/:id/backfill?from_seq=) to allow clients to request missing sequences when resume happens after TTL.
4) Add defensive handling for truncated JSON/chunk edges: attempt auto-complete of final token when safe and mark stream as truncated with a stable error code so clients can trigger backfill.
5) Tune CloudLB and gateway keepalive and increase default idle timeout to 5 minutes for streaming routes, and document recommend proxy config for Dedicated/Private customers.
rollout_plan:
- Merge changes behind feature flag 'stable-resume-v2' in runtime-1.21 branch.
- Canary deploy: 5% of hosted traffic to edge nodes running feature flag. Monitor resume success rate and error classes for 48h.
- If metrics stable, increase to 25% for 24h, then 100% rollout the flag.
- Coordinate with Dedicated/Private ops to provide config diff and recommend upgrade window; offer assisted upgrade for customers on older control-plane.
- Communicate to customers via status page and targeted emails with recommended HA proxy and CloudLB settings.
qa_and_validation:
- Integration tests to simulate mid-chunk drops and verify resume succeeds across sequence gaps.
- Fuzz tests for resume token tampering and race reconnect scenarios.
- End-to-end validation using the reproducer harness against staging and a dedicated canary customer with large outputs.
- Add regression tests asserting no duplicate tokens accepted beyond configured dedupe window.
- Manual verification checklist for SRE to run post-rollout.
postmortem_actions: Document recommended proxy keepalive/idle timeout in Hosted docs and Dedicated upgrade guide
Add alert on abnormal rate of 'resume_token_mismatch' errors and sudden spike in truncated_stream events
Build small persistent resume cache with metrics (hit/miss) and instrument TTL expiration reasons
Run quarterly chaos test in staging for streaming: random mid-chunk connection kills
